Ukraine confronts labor shortage as need for soldiers drains workforce  Were it not for Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, however, Tatyiana Ustymenko wouldn’t have this job. The coal mine in Pavlohrad allowed women to work underground for the first time in its history only after Russia invaded in February 2022. It was desperate to fill the many vacancies left by men who joined the military.  The mine is not the only workplace experiencing a critical labor shortage. Online job portals in Ukraine say they have never advertised so many openings. Millions of Ukrainians moved abroad to escape Moscow’s brutal bombardment, and of those who stayed, hundreds of thousands of men have traded their jobs for military service.  Now, with Kyiv ramping up its mobilization efforts, businesses expect that workers will be even harder to find, further straining Ukraine’s crippled economy. With more openings than jobseekers, many businesses have had to raise wages to compete — or they risk shutting down.  Read the full story here.

Today, with the ascension of the family of the late Rani Goili to the grave at the end of the seven days, one of the most terrible and painful periods the people of Israel have known ends. The family, friends, comrades-in-arms and Israeli police officers and many others gathered this morning at the fresh grave of Rani Goili, a hero of Israel and defender of the unknown.   Rani, the last remaining abductee in Gaza, was finally laid to rest - not as we had hoped, but as it had to happen: at home, on his land, surrounded by the love of his family and people.  This is a moment of deep mourning, but also of closing a painful national circle. 255 abductees were returned to Israel. 87 were placed as victims, each one a world and full, each of them an open wound in the hearts of the families and in the heart of the entire country.  The headquarters of the families for the return of the abductees ends its activity with a sense of unrelenting pain for all those who could be with us here today and are not, but also with a clear knowledge: the struggle was waged in the name of the values ​​of the State of Israel and the people of Israel. The values ​​of mutual guarantee, social solidarity and the duty to return home every abductee regardless of religion, race and gender, soldiers and civilians, living or dead.   This historic struggle for their return will be engraved in the national memory as a reminder of the unimaginable human cost of October 7, and of the deep commitment of Israeli society to the families, the missing and the missing. It was also the beautiful hour of the people of Israel who took to the streets en masse, all over the country in the name of these values.  On this day, we will also cherish the soldiers and women of the IDF and all the security forces for a very long and bloody fight. We will send a blessing of recovery to all those wounded in body and soul and we will forever be grateful to all the bereaved families who lost the most precious to them of all. We bow our heads to the Goyili family and to all the families of the martyrs, and pray that we will never have to fight like this again. The General Secretariat of the Arab National Congress mourned the martyrdom of Ali Larijani, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, who, along with his son and several companions, were "killed in a cowardly operation carried out by the Zionist enemy."  The statement emphasized that the "enemy mistakenly believed that assassinating senior leaders would achieve its aggressive objectives, not realizing that such crimes would only strengthen the resolve of the struggling Iranian people in defending their land, sovereignty, and dignity."  The Arab National Congress also extended its "deepest condolences to the Islamic Republic of Iran and its people," praising Larijani as an "eminent leader" who dedicated his life to defending his nation, supporting freedom worldwide, and standing steadfast with "the Palestinian people, their just cause, and their heroic Resistance."
